
Scanned Grok social signals and arXiv RSS signals. Most Grok signals reference papers with fabricated/unverifiable arXiv IDs or are already covered by existing README entries. One arXiv RSS signal stands out: a transformer applied to wildlife movement trajectory classification — a genuine non-NLP domain application with measurable classification performance on sensor/GPS data. The antibody sequence generation paper also merits consideration for the Biology & Genomics section. The remaining signals are either NLP-adjacent, unverifiable, or too weak.

## Suggestions

- [Transformer-Based Wildlife Species Classification from Daily Movement Trajectories](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06726) — Applies transformer architecture to GPS/accelerometer movement trajectories for wildlife species classification, demonstrating benchmark performance on ecological sensor data.
  Section: Time-Series & Signals | Criteria: Applies transformer architecture to a non-NLP domain (ecological movement/sensor signals), Addresses a domain-specific classification task with measurable performance, Iterative training loop grounded in temporal movement trajectory data, Empirical outcome demonstrating advantage of transformer approach on species classification benchmark

- [Conditional generation of antibody sequences with classifier-guided germline-absorbing discrete diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06720) — Transformer-based discrete diffusion model for conditional antibody sequence generation guided by germline structure, with empirical evaluation on sequence quality and developability metrics.
  Section: Biology & Genomics | Criteria: Applies transformer/attention architecture to a non-NLP domain (immunology/antibody design), Addresses domain-specific generation task with measurable performance (sequence quality, developability), Iterative training loop grounded in antibody sequence data, Empirical outcome demonstrating advantage over baseline generative approaches
